- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes — cap forecast growth after 2–3 consecutive high sentiment days.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >5% daily increase), model often lags — adjust forecast to anticipate 1–2 day lead in price rise.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) — apply downward correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model often misjudges direction — align forecast with sentiment trend shift, not peak.
